Value set at $4.4M/acre = upper end of the typical current range for a large assembled DC site, not the $3.76M assessment average (method says do not use averages) and not the $6.34M record outlier. tax_abatement_years.method: Virginia / Loudoun. INSTRUMENT: retail SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on data center equipment (Va. Code Sec. 58.1-609.3(18)), not a property tax abatement. The exemption is not a fixed number of years: VEDP states it runs 'from the date of the data center's MOU through June 30, 2035', so the term is the remaining life of the program at the date the qualifying MOU is signed. An MOU executed in 2026 therefore yields ~9 years (value = 2035 sunset minus 2026), which is why basis is modeled rather than sourced. Thresholds (150M USD capex / 50 jobs at 150% of local average wage; 70M USD / 10 jobs in distressed localities from 1 Jul 2023) must generally be met within 3 years of the MOU. High end of 24 years = MOUs signed on or after 1 Jan 2023 that commit 100B USD capex and 2,500 jobs, which extend the exemption to 2050 (35B USD / 1,000 jobs extends to 2040). Cross-checked against the Virginia Dept of Taxation report to the General Assembly dated 2 Jan 2026 (https://rga.lis.virginia.gov/Published/2026/RD40/PDF), which reports 56 companies claiming the exemption in FY2025 but does not state a per-facility term.

water_rate_usd_per_kgal.method: San Antonio Water System, General Class (commercial/industrial). SAWS splits the volumetric water charge across two separate published schedules and both must be added. (1) Water Delivery, general-class page, 'Effective for Consumption on or about January 1, 2026', inside city: base block (up to 100% of the customer's annual average monthly use) $1.958 per 1,000 gal; then $2.252 (>100-125%), $2.937 (>125-175%), $3.427 (>175%). (2) General Class Water Supply Fee, base block $3.079 per 1,000 gal (then $3.541 / $4.619 / $5.389). Sum of the base blocks = 1.958 + 3.079 = $5.037, rounded to 5.04 per 1,000 gal. Both components are already per 1,000 gallons; no unit conversion. Used the BASE block because SAWS defines blocks as a percentage of the customer's own prior-year average month, not fixed gallons - a flat-load data center sits in its own base block essentially all year and never escalates. The supply fee is larger than the delivery charge, so reading only the general-class page would understate water cost by about 61%. Basis is modeled because the two components carry different vintages: the delivery page states January 1, 2026 while the water supply fee page's table is labeled 2024 under a legacy 'effective January 1, 2023' heading, so the sum is not a single as-published number. Wastewater is billed on the same volume, flat across all usage, at $4.3680 per 1,000 gal inside city (2026), which nearly doubles the volumetric bill to about $9.41.

Converted 6.16/0.748 = 8.24 per 1,000 gal. Basis is modeled, not sourced, because the figure is (a) from a news page rather than the tariff and (b) carried forward to today on the utility's 'no increase since 2012' statement, which leaves a possible 2012 step unaccounted for. Sewer is billed on the same metered water volume and is roughly 2.5x the water rate ($15.69/CCF = $20.98 per 1,000 gal), so the combined volumetric cost is far larger than the water line alone - Atlanta commonly publishes water and sewer combined, and that combined figure was deliberately NOT used here. Ignored cleanwateratlanta.h2o4atl.com: confirmed dead, now serving gambling spam.

land_cost_per_acre_usd.method: Aggregate of live listings (source type c). LandSearch Georgia statewide, tag=industrial, size min 10 acres = 116 listings; filtered by hand to metro Atlanta counties (Fulton, DeKalb, Cobb, Gwinnett, Clayton, Coweta, Barrow) = 7 listings: Winder (Barrow) 29.1ac $27,317; Suwanee (Gwinnett) 61.3ac $35,564; Newnan (Coweta) 11.5ac $57,878; Lithonia (DeKalb) 17.7ac $113,011; Jonesboro (Clayton) 10.8ac $342,593; Newnan (Coweta) 13.7ac $430,657; Duluth (Gwinnett) 18.6ac $537,634. Low and high are the min and max of those 7. Value=$430,657 = upper end of the typical range for an infill/near-in metro industrial site; the Duluth $537,634 is the single dearest and is held as high rather than value. County-level LandSearch and Fulton County queries returned zero 10+ acre industrial listings, so the state-filtered query was used. Asking prices, hence modeled.

construction_cost_per_kw.method: Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition), market chart on the Data centre cost trends page. Market row 'Atlanta' = US$9.9045/W. Conversion: 9.9045 x 1000 = 9904.5, rounded to 9905 USD per kW of IT load.

tax_rate.method: Atlanta / Fulton County GA. Fulton County Tax Commissioner's published millage rate history table, 2025 row: City of Atlanta millage 31.870 mills (this column includes the Atlanta Public Schools levy) + Fulton County millage in City of Atlanta 9.039 mills = TOTAL 40.909 mills. Georgia assesses real property at 40% of fair market value. Arithmetic: 40.909/1000 x 0.40 = 0.0163636, rounded 0.0164. CAVEAT ON TRACEABILITY: the 40% assessment ratio is the standard Georgia statutory ratio (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7) but is NOT printed on the millage-rate PDF cited here; I was unable to open a separate page stating it before exhausting the web-search budget. The millage total itself is read directly off the cited document.

tax_abatement_years.method: Georgia / Atlanta. INSTRUMENT: state and local SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on data center equipment (high-technology data center exemption, O.C.G.A. Sec. 48-8-3(68.1)) - an equipment exemption, not a property tax abatement. Georgia Dept of Audits and Accounts tax incentive evaluation (Dec 2022) states 'Data centers must meet the investment threshold within seven years of their exemption start date', which is the operative term of a certificate; thresholds are tiered by county population (25M USD under 30,000; 75M USD for 30,000-50,000; 250M USD over 50,000 - Fulton/DeKalb/Douglas etc. in the Atlanta market fall in the 250M USD tier). SUNSET: sources conflict and this matters. The 2022 audit says the exemption sunsets in 2033 (as extended by HB 1291, 2022); Alston and Bird, 12 Feb 2026 (https://www.alston.com/en/insights/publications/2026/02/georgia-sales-tax-exemptions-data-centers) states it 'is set to expire on December 31, 2031'; NCSL (1 Apr 2026) says 2032. Treat the sunset as 2031-2033 and note that five 2026 bills (SB 408, SB 410, SB 436, HB 559, HB 1012) would repeal, suspend or pause it.

Converted at 1 CCF = 748 gal: summer 4.18/0.748 = 5.59 (high), winter 2.58/0.748 = 3.45 (low). value is the simple unweighted mean of the two seasonal rates ((4.18+2.58)/2 = 3.38 per CCF = 4.52 per 1,000 gal) - basis is modeled because of that averaging, not because of the unit conversion. water_rate_usd_per_kgal.method: Metropolitan Utilities District of Omaha, Rate Schedule W-3 Large Volume Industrial Water Service, effective January 2, 2026 (linked from https://www.mudomaha.com/rates-fees/). W-3 is a declining block: the first 5,000 CCF or less is a LUMP SUM of $11,456.00 (not a per-unit rate), and the marginal rate over 5,000 CCF is $1.9657 per CCF. Took the marginal over-5,000-CCF rate: 1.9657/0.748 = 2.63 per 1,000 gal (schedule states 1 CCF = 748 gal). Did not divide the lump sum by anything - at exactly 5,000 CCF it implies $2.29/CCF, and dividing it by any other volume gives a wrong number. Which schedule a data center actually qualifies for: W-3 requires an industrial process user with normal consumption of 5,000+ CCF/month and a one-year commitment, and explicitly excludes irrigation; W-4 is 'available to AND REQUIRED OF' commercial and industrial customers buying water primarily for sprinkling, lake/lagoon recharge and/or COOLING. A data center whose load is chiefly evaporative cooling would therefore be pushed onto W-4, whose over-1,100-CCF block is $2.0093 per CCF Nov-May ($2.69 per 1,000 gal) and $4.0350 per CCF Jun-Oct ($5.39 per 1,000 gal) - materially worse in summer. W-2 (general commercial/industrial) is $2.0309 per CCF Nov-May and $2.7187 Jun-Oct ($2.71 / $3.63 per 1,000 gal). Value reported is W-3 as instructed; treat W-4 as the realistic downside. A $11,456 minimum monthly commodity charge plus a meter service charge (up to $1,405/mo at 12-inch) applies under W-3, and a 2% statutory payment applies inside city/village limits. Sewer is set by the City of Omaha, not MUD, and is not included.

tax_rate.method: Dublin IE. THE TAX MEASURED IS COMMERCIAL RATES (local authority rates), not a value-based property tax. Dublin City Council page: 'Commercial rates are calculated by multiplying the Rateable Valuation of your property by a multiplier called the Annual Rate on Valuation (ARV)'; ARV for 2025 = 0.282, with worked example Rateable Valuation EUR 10,000 x 0.282 = EUR 2,820. ASSUMPTION: 5.5% net initial yield (capitalisation rate) for Dublin industrial/data-centre property, so capital value = annual rent / 0.055. Arithmetic: 0.282 x 0.055 = 0.01551, rounded 0.0155. Low/high bracket the yield at 4.5% (0.282 x 0.045 = 0.0127) and 6.5% (0.282 x 0.065 = 0.0183). A data centre in Fingal or South Dublin County Council territory would use that authority's ARV instead, which differs from Dublin City's.

water_rate_usd_per_kgal.method: THIS IS A WHOLESALE PRICE, NOT A RETAIL PRICE. England's non-household water market has been fully competitive since 2017, so the price a Slough data centre actually pays is a negotiated retail contract that is not published anywhere; I could not find any published retail tariff. Slough sits in Thames Water's supply area, so I used Thames Water's 'Indicative wholesale charges schedule 2026-27', effective 1 April 2026, which I opened and read. Non-household metered potable water volumetric bands: 0-20,000 m3 272.07 p/m3 (NHHMPW1-4); 20,000-50,000 m3 248.94 p/m3; 50,000-250,000 m3 204.05 p/m3; OVER 250,000 m3 163.24 p/m3 (NHHMPW7). Declining block, so value = bottom block 163.24 p/m3 = GBP 1.6324/m3. Conversion: 1.6324 / 0.74691 GBP-per-USD = USD 2.1855/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 8.27 per 1,000 US gal. 'high' = the smallest-user band 272.07 p/m3 -> USD 13.79/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/GBP 0.74691, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. Basis is 'modeled' because wholesale is being substituted for retail: a retailer adds a gross margin (typically low single-digit % of the wholesale charge) plus the retailer's own fixed fees, so true retail is somewhat above this. Large users also pay flat annual supplementary charges (intermediate GBP 4,626 / large GBP 27,071 / super-large GBP 129,096) that are not volumetric. WASTEWATER: billed on the same metered volume - non-household metered foul-drainage wholesale volumetric charge is 156.61 p/m3 for standard bands, falling to 125.28 p/m3 for users over 100,000 m3 (plus a GBP 29,756 annual supplementary charge). 125.28 p/m3 = USD 6.35 per 1,000 US gal, so sewer adds roughly 75% on top of the water rate for a large site.

land_cost_per_acre_usd.method: Knight Frank Industrial Land Values Research 2022. Slough is named and priced on the page: average industrial land value GBP 3.46m per acre, Q1 2022 (up GBP 1.76m / 103% since Q1 2019), and Slough is the highest of all South East local authorities listed. Value = GBP 3,460,000/acre x 1.338849 = USD 4,632,419/acre. low = GBP 2.51m/acre (Welwyn Hatfield, the lowest South East authority in the same table) = USD 3,360,512; high = Slough's own GBP 3.46m. Other SE points on the page for context: Spelthorne GBP 3.42m, Runnymede GBP 3.41m, Thurrock GBP 3.03m, South Buckinghamshire GBP 2.64m. Values are modelled by Knight Frank on a standardised 20,000 sq m warehouse, i.e. large-parcel basis. Freehold. FX: 1 GBP = 1.338849 USD (USD/GBP 0.74691), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. On the MHCLG/DLUHC route: I found the current dataset (gov.uk/government/publications/land-value-estimates-for-policy-appraisal-2023, valuation date 1 Oct 2023) but the per-authority industrial figures live only in the .xlsx/.ods attachments, which are binary and could not be opened by any available fetch tool; the HTML 'guidelines for use' page confirms 119 industrial valuations were done but prints no local-authority table, and the 2015 PDF prints only an England mean (GBP 482,000/ha). Cross-check on order of magnitude: Colliers (colliers.com/en-gb/news/25-03-22-industrial-land-values-are-reaching-record-levels-in-london-and-south-east) puts South East industrial land at GBP 2.5m/acre and London at GBP 7.1m/acre on Jan 2022 data. Both sources are 2022 - UK industrial land has moved since, so this is a floor, not a current quote.

tax_rate.method: Slough UK. THE TAX MEASURED IS NON-DOMESTIC RATES (business rates), not a value-based property tax. Bill = rateable value x multiplier. GOV.UK gives the England multipliers for the 2026 to 2027 rating year: standard multiplier 48 pence in the pound (rateable value GBP 51,000 and above), small business multiplier 43.2 pence. A data centre exceeds GBP 51,000 RV, so the standard 0.48 multiplier applies. Slough Borough Council is a unitary billing authority applying the national multiplier. Rateable value is an estimate of ANNUAL RENTAL value - GOV.UK: 'its open market rental value on 1 April 2024, based on an estimate by the Valuation Office' (the 2026 rating list). Converting to an effective rate on CAPITAL value therefore requires a yield assumption. ASSUMPTION: 5.5% net initial yield for Thames Valley / Slough Trading Estate industrial and data-centre property, i.e. capital value = annual rent / 0.055. Arithmetic: 0.48 x 0.055 = 0.0264. Low/high bracket the yield at 4.5% (0.48 x 0.045 = 0.0216) and 6.5% (0.48 x 0.065 = 0.0312). Transitional relief and any empty-property or improvement relief are ignored. Same yield assumption used for row 39 (Dublin) so the two annual-value regimes are treated consistently.

water_rate_usd_per_kgal.method: Eau de Paris 'Catalogue des tarifs 2026', opened directly; tariffs effective 1 January 2026. Eau de Paris publishes ONE volumetric tariff - there is no separate tarif non-domestique and no volume blocks, so a large industrial user pays the same per-m3 as everyone else (only the part fixe / abonnement varies with meter size). Value = the all-in WATER-side volumetric total, summing the components printed in the catalogue (all EUR/m3 TTC): fourniture d'eau potable 1.1942 + redevance soutien d'etiage 0.0074 + redevance prelevement sur la ressource en eau 0.0928 + redevance Voies Navigables de France 0.0169 + redevance performance reseaux d'eau potable 0.0406 + redevance consommation d'eau (Agence de l'eau Seine-Normandie) 0.3587 = EUR 1.7106/m3. Conversion: 1.7106 / 0.87138 = USD 1.9633/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 7.43 per 1,000 US gal. 'low' = the bare fourniture d'eau potable 1.1942 -> USD 5.19/kgal. 'high' = the complete bill including assainissement -> EUR 4.2142/m3 -> USD 18.31/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/EUR 0.87138, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. Basis 'modeled' because the value is a sum of six separately-printed line items, not a single figure read off the page. WASTEWATER: billed on exactly the same metered volume and it is the larger half of the bill - collecte des eaux usees (Ville de Paris / SAP) EUR 0.6699/m3, transport et epuration (SIAAP) EUR 1.6984/m3, redevance performance reseaux de collecte EUR 0.1353/m3, total EUR 2.5036/m3 = USD 10.88 per 1,000 US gal. Figures are TTC (5.5% VAT on water supply, 10% on assainissement); a business recovers VAT, so net-of-VAT costs are ~5% lower. Cross-check: Eau de Paris's own price page (https://www.eaudeparis.fr/prix-de-leau) quotes EUR 4.23 TTC/m3 all-in for 2026, consistent with the EUR 4.2142 sum above.

land_cost_per_acre_usd.method: Arthur Loyd Ile-de-France land-for-sale listings (live, current asking prices), industrial/artisanal-use terrains. Parcels of 1 ha or more on that page: 39,269 m2 at EUR 734,853 = EUR 18.71/m2 (Seine-et-Marne); 19,871 m2 at EUR 1,390,970 = EUR 70.00/m2 (Seine-et-Marne); 14,677 m2 at EUR 1,050,000 = EUR 71.54/m2 (Villiers-en-Biere); 13,443 m2 at EUR 2,000,000 = EUR 148.78/m2 (Montereau-Fault-Yonne). Value = upper end EUR 148.78/m2 x 4046.86 = EUR 602,090/acre x 1.147605 = USD 690,964/acre. low = EUR 18.71/m2 = USD 86,907/acre. Smaller inner-ring plots on the same page run higher (Lisses 5,000 m2 at EUR 300/m2, Saint-Soupplets 5,704 m2 at EUR 280/m2), which a 10-acre-plus site would not reach. Cross-check: solumat.fr (dated 3 Jun 2026) prints a France-wide industrial land average of EUR 120/m2 in 2026 with a range of EUR 15-150/m2, consistent with the Ile-de-France upper end used here. FX: 1 EUR = 1.147605 USD (USD/EUR 0.87138), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold. Basis modeled: asking prices from listings, per-m2 rates derived by me from price divided by surface. Only one listing exceeded 10 acres (the 39,269 m2 / 9.7-acre Seine-et-Marne parcel), so the large-parcel sample is thin; bureauxlocaux.com had a single 62,000 m2 industrial parcel in Ile-de-France (Ribecourt-Dreslincourt) but priced 'nous consulter'.

Singapore's non-domestic tariff is flat - there are no consumption blocks. I found no evidence of a further revision taking effect in 2026, so the 1 April 2025 rates are current. Conversion: 3.24 / 1.2875 SGD-per-USD = USD 2.5165/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 9.53 per 1,000 US gal. 'low' = tariff + WCT only (S$2.15, i.e. excluding the waterborne/used-water element) -> USD 6.32/kgal. NEWATER (reclaimed - what a Singapore data centre would actually buy for cooling): from 1 April 2025, Tariff 1.28 + WCT 0.13 + Waterborne 1.09 = TOTAL S$2.50/m3 before GST = USD 7.35 per 1,000 US gal, about 23% cheaper than potable. Source: JTC 'Historical data on IGLS sites sold by JTC' (Industrial Government Land Sales), file dated 26 Jun 2026. Value = Plot B Tukang Innovation Drive, awarded 8 Oct 2025, site area 18,722.2 m2, 33-year lease, successful tender SGD 95,188,888 = SGD 5,084.28 per m2 of SITE area (the file's own price column is per m2 per plot ratio at PR 2.5, i.e. SGD 2,033.71 - I divided total price by land area to get a land rate). SGD 5,084.28/m2 x 4046.86 = SGD 20,575,414/acre x 0.776699 = USD 15,980,178/acre. low = Plot A Tuas Bay Drive, awarded 14 Nov 2025, 6,338.1 m2, 23-year lease, SGD 4,885,000 = SGD 770.74/m2 = USD 2,422,584/acre. Other western-industrial comparables from the same file: Penjuru Road 23 Jan 2026, 20,852.9 m2, 33 yr, SGD 87,400,890 = SGD 4,191.31/m2; Pioneer Road 28 Aug 2025, 28,058.4 m2, 33 yr, SGD 88,190,020 = SGD 3,143.09/m2; Gul Drive 20 Jun 2025, 4,876.3 m2, 23 yr = SGD 984.51/m2. water_rate_usd_per_kgal.method: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Waterworks. The Bureau's own rate pages (waterworks.metro.tokyo.lg.jp) return HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so I read the statutory tariff table in the Tokyo Metropolitan Water Supply Ordinance (Toukyou-to kyuusui jourei) on the TMG regulations site, which I opened successfully. Steeply INCREASING block tariff, so per the rule I took the TOP block. Juuryou ryoukin (volumetric), yen/m3: 5-10 m3 22; 10-20 m3 128; 20-30 m3 163; 30-50 m3 202; 50-100 m3 213; 100-200 m3 298; 200-1,000 m3 372; OVER 1,000 m3 404. A data centre is unambiguously in the over-1,000 m3 top block. Kihon ryoukin (fixed monthly charge) scales with meter diameter for a large-diameter service: 100mm JPY 94,568; 150mm JPY 159,094; 200mm JPY 349,434; 250mm JPY 480,135; 300mm and above JPY 816,145 per month - fixed, not volumetric, so excluded from the per-gallon rate. The ordinance states the tabulated amounts are the base multiplied by 110/100, i.e. they INCLUDE 10% consumption tax. Value uses the published tax-inclusive JPY 404/m3: 404 / 162.94 JPY-per-USD = USD 2.4794/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 9.39 per 1,000 US gal. tax_rate.method: Sao Paulo BR. THE TAX MEASURED IS IPTU (Imposto Predial e Territorial Urbano), levied on the valor venal (assessed market value) of the property. Base aliquota for built NON-RESIDENTIAL property, Lei Municipal 6.989/1966 art. 8 as amended by Lei 13.250/2001: 'O imposto calcula-se a razao de 1,5% sobre o valor venal do imovel, para imoveis construidos com utilizacao diversa da referida no artigo 7' (residential is 1.0% under art. 7). That base rate is then adjusted by the value-band desconto/acrescimo table of Lei 15.889/2013 art. 4 (https://legislacao.prefeitura.sp.gov.br/leis/lei-15889-de-05-de-novembro-de-2013), which for non-residential property reads: up to R$150,000 -0.4%; R$150,000-300,000 -0.2%; R$300,000-600,000 0.0%; R$600,000-1,200,000 +0.2%; above R$1,200,000 +0.4%. A data centre sits far above the top band, so the applicable effective aliquota = 1.5% + 0.4% = 1.9% of valor venal. Value 0.0190; low 0.0110 is the smallest-property case (1.5% - 0.4%), high 0.0190 the large-property case. Valor venal is the municipality's Planta Generica de Valores assessment, which typically runs below open-market value, so the rate on true market value is somewhat lower. last_verified is the year of the governing amending law (Lei 15.889/2013); the source pages give no tax year.

A data centre enrolled in the programme therefore pays the Block 2 rate, which is 32% below Block 1; if it is NOT enrolled it pays Block 1 on everything, which is why Block 1 is recorded as 'high'. Value = CAD 3.3219/m3 (on-time payment; late payment adds 5.26%). Conversion: 3.3219 / 1.4046 CAD-per-USD = USD 2.3650/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 8.95 per 1,000 US gal. 'high' = Block 1 CAD 4.8629/m3 -> USD 13.11 per 1,000 US gal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/CAD 1.4046, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. The Block 1 / Block 2 consumption rates are the consumption charge shown on the Toronto utility bill; I did not find a second per-m3 sewer line item to add, so no sewer number is claimed here.
